title: One owner for lane state and a typed ship verdict (ADR 0022 amendment, 9 slices)
body:
Source: Fable architecture review .krn/runs/arch-review/architecture.md (sections 2-4) and history review .krn/runs/arch-review/history.md (class 2: 10 fixes / 1221 lines; class 3: 10 / 607).
Evidence: "is this lane merged" has eight implementations (src/cli/lane.ts:219-243,303-370; src/hook/stop.ts:1464-1532; src/ci/ship.ts:371-447). The ship result is text that lane-run parses (src/cli/lane-run/verdict.ts:369, drain.ts:23-28), so ship's exit code and gate reason are lost. shipRun is one 753-line function; ship.ts grew from 230 to 1108 lines in six days against ADR 0022's thin-ship target. 143 fixes in 30 days, against a goal of under 10.
Files: src/lane/ (new owner), src/ci/ship.ts, src/cli/lane.ts, src/cli/lane-run/*, src/hook/stop.ts, docs/adr (amend ADR 0022 first)
Outcome: amend ADR 0022 with the recommended design from the report. One module owns lane state (worktree, claim, ship record, merged status) and has a typed state. Ship returns a typed verdict with its exit code. Post-merge effects leave ship. Migrate in the report's 9 PR-sized slices, each a follow-up task linked with --after.
Proof: the ADR amendment is merged; the follow-up tasks exist; slice 1's property test over the lane state type passes.
